source_artifacts.claim: Current room defines ferry/stop, island, short unstable bridge, steady/rescue handoff, lethal slime below ferry and bridge, optional collectibles and exits.
Hold-pad effects depend on occupancy; an unstable bridge collapses after its authored duration when unsteady and later resets.
Contact with an active hazard that harms both causes death.
Gem bubbles temporarily FLOAT Isp or make Pac STICKY; rescue interrupts the bubble.
Villain scene associates Gem’s bubble with bridge instability and Cana’s finish gate with rescue counter.
Earlier level 03 teaches Isp STOP to brake ferry, bubble can float him off, rebrake and Pac ferry/rescue route.
Earlier level 04 teaches Pac holding STEADY for Isp to cross and activate RESCUE.
Roster order puts levels 02,01,04,03,37,45,06,08,34 before level05 at position 10.

prior_knowledge.concept: Pac holds STEADY while Isp crosses an unstable bridge and reaches RESCUE, which keeps the bridge stable.

evidence.claim: Level 04 introduces Pac’s steady role and Isp’s rescue handoff over an unstable bridge.

evidence.claim: Level 02 introduces bubble interference and rescue interruption; previous opportunity does not imply practiced skill.

mechanics.fact: Pac-only STEADY stabilizes the 0.8-second unstable bridge and opens isp_bridge while held; Isp-only RESCUE latches, stabilizes the bridge, and opens the remaining gates so Pac can follow.

evidence.claim: Bridge collapse period, hold role, rescue latch and gate effects.

evidence.claim: Current level defines a bubble attack and rescue interruption.

legal_routes.name: Isp brakes, Pac steadies, Isp rescues, Pac follows

steps.goal: Stop the ferry and open Pac’s crossing to the island.
steps.action: Move to STOP on the safe start shore and occupy it; when Gem’s bubble floats Isp off the pad, land and return to STOP.
steps.expected_feedback: STOP turns off the ferry motor and opens pac_island while Isp occupies it; bubble interference can temporarily release the pad.
steps.observed_feedback: The current route first shows STOP active, then Isp airborne with STOP inactive, then STOP active again at frame 796.

evidence.claim: Isp-only STOP uses hold activation to motor-stop ferry and open pac_island.
Bubble attack can disrupt stop holder and rescue interrupts it.
At frame 38 Isp occupies STOP and pac_island is open.
At frame 241 Isp is floating/off STOP and Pac has reached the island.
At frame 796 STOP is active again after Isp returns.

steps.goal: Cross the ferry gap to island and hold STEADY to stabilize the bridge/open Isp’s bridge gate.
steps.action: Board/cross the ferry and reach the island; stand on Pac-only STEADY while Isp approaches and crosses the bridge.
steps.expected_feedback: STEADY stabilizes the bridge and opens isp_bridge while Pac holds it.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1121 Pac occupies STEADY and isp_bridge is open.

evidence.claim: Ferry connects start to island; Pac STEADY stabilizes bridge and opens Isp gate.
At frame 1121 Pac occupies STEADY and the Isp bridge gate is open.

steps.goal: Cross the bridge while Pac holds STEADY and activate RESCUE on the far side.
steps.action: Traverse the ferry/island approach, then cross the bridge; continue all the way to RESCUE rather than treating first contact with the bridge as the handoff point.
steps.expected_feedback: RESCUE latches, stabilizes bridge, opens Pac’s finish barrier and keeps Isp’s bridge route open; it interrupts Gem’s bubble.
steps.observed_feedback: The completed current-source route shows RESCUE latched and all gates open by frame 1761; the separate early-release test shows a premature Pac departure after Isp first lands on bridge causes collapse and death.

evidence.claim: Isp RESCUE is a latch that stabilizes bridge and opens remaining gates.
At frame 1761 RESCUE is latched and all gates are open.
The early-release trigger records Isp first supported on bridge while Pac still holds STEADY; the instruction’s handoff is later, at Isp pressing RESCUE.

steps.goal: Follow Isp across the stabilized bridge and reach orange exit.
steps.action: Keep STEADY active until Isp presses RESCUE; after the latch takes over bridge stability, leave the pad, cross the bridge, then reach Pac’s exit.
steps.expected_feedback: Rescue remains latched, bridge remains safe, and Pac’s finish gate opens for the follow-through.
steps.observed_feedback: The accepted current-source route completes with both exits and no deaths at frame 2425; Pac releasing 39 frames after Isp first boards the bridge instead causes the bridge to collapse and Isp to die.

evidence.claim: Subtitle and hint specify the precise handoff; rescue latch stabilizes bridge and opens Pac finish.
Accepted route reference reaches complete.
Premature release after bridge boarding ends dead, showing that the handoff is not first bridge contact.

Current-source replay first completes at frame 2425 with zero deaths.
A separate early-release error test fails, showing the correct hold-to-rescue handoff is required.

isp: Hold STOP to brake ferry/open Pac access, re-establish STOP if a bubble floats him off.
Cross to the far side and reach RESCUE; keep moving past initial bridge contact until the latch activates.
Use the rescue latch to keep bridge safe and open Pac’s finish route, then reach blue exit.
pac: Cross the ferry gap to island and hold STEADY to stabilize the bridge/open Isp’s bridge barrier.
Keep holding until Isp reaches RESCUE, then leave and follow across the bridge to orange exit.

common_mistakes.mistake: Gem’s bubble floats Isp off STOP before Pac reaches island.
common_mistakes.consequence: The pad releases, ferry motor can restart, and pac_island closes until STOP is reactivated.
common_mistakes.recovery: Let Isp land and reoccupy STOP; the source hint calls out this cycle and the ordinary route shows Isp re-establishing STOP. No lethal reset is implied by this pad release alone.

evidence.claim: Hint says Gem sweeps STOP and Isp re-brakes; pad hold opens Pac gate.
Isp is off STOP after a bubble; later the pad is reactivated at frame 796.
STOP active again before the bridge phase.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac leaves STEADY when Isp first boards the bridge instead of waiting for Isp to press RESCUE.
common_mistakes.consequence: After 39 frames the bridge begins accumulating unsupported occupancy, collapses at about 0.8 seconds, and Isp falls into bridge slime and dies.
common_mistakes.recovery: Do not leave until Isp reaches RESCUE. If the bridge collapses after the safe transfer is no longer available, the attempt is dead and requires a full restart; if nobody is lost and it resets, re-stabilize before crossing. The deliberate early-release trace demonstrates the fatal version.

evidence.claim: Visible subtitle specifies hold until Isp presses RESCUE; bridge timer and hazard location.
At frame 1549 Isp first stands on bridge, Pac still holds STEADY.
At frame 1588 Pac has left STEADY; bridge is no longer stabilized.
At frame 1751 Isp is dead after bridge collapse.

common_mistakes.mistake: A hero misses the ferry or bridge landing and falls into the underlying slime.
common_mistakes.consequence: The authored slime harms both, so contact kills and resets the attempt.
common_mistakes.recovery: Retry from the start shore and re-establish STOP/STEADY; the ferry route and bridge handoff must be repeated. The accepted route did not contain such a fall, so this consequence is source-inferred.

evidence.claim: Ferry/bridge geometry and slime below both mandatory spans.
Active hazard contact is lethal.

common_mistakes.mistake: Pac reads first bridge contact as enough and leaves the hold early.
common_mistakes.consequence: Isp can progress partway before bridge collapse, so the error is delayed and may look safe at first; then the bridge disappears while he is still over slime.
common_mistakes.recovery: Use the explicit visible handoff instruction as condition: continue holding until Isp presses RESCUE, not merely steps onto the bridge. A completed reference route confirms success after correct handoff.

evidence.claim: Start screen explicitly says Pac holds STEADY until Isp presses RESCUE.
Early release begins the bridge collapse sequence.
Current-source ordinary-input reference route completes both exits in 2425 frames without death; it is a feasibility result, not a human learning outcome.

optional_collectibles: orange_island (Pac) and blue_bridge (Isp) are optional; neither lies on the required exit condition.

reasoning.rationale: The full route chains Isp’s STOP, Pac’s ferry crossing and STEADY hold, Isp’s bridge crossing to RESCUE, then Pac’s follow-through. Bubble displacement can undo the first hold and force a re-brake; premature bridge handoff creates a lethal collapse. The explicit subtitle/hint state the intended roles, but the route still has multiple dependent state changes.

evidence.claim: Hint and pad effects establish the ordered route.
Isp stop opens Pac’s gate.
Pac holds bridge state.
Isp rescue latch transfers bridge safety and opens remaining gates.
Premature release creates a distinct failure dependency.

cooperation.rationale: The route has multiple necessary contributions: Isp brakes the ferry, Pac crosses and holds STEADY, Isp must reach RESCUE, and Pac follows only after the latch. This is repeated mutual dependency and a precise handoff, not merely both heroes traveling separately.

evidence.claim: Isp stop, Pac steady, Isp rescue are separate pad roles.
Visible subtitle and hint state Pac must hold until Isp presses RESCUE.
Isp rescue is latched before Pac leaves STEADY and follows.

execution.rationale: Both heroes must traverse a moving ferry crossing and the long bridge span over slime; Pac maintains a hold while Isp threads across to a far rescue, then makes the bridge crossing himself. Several jump/landing transitions are required, and the current route completes without death, showing feasibility rather than low novice error rates.

evidence.claim: Moving ferry, island, bridge, finish and separate exits define movement.
Pac jumps onto the ferry route.
Isp completes the bridge/rescue route.
Pac follows across bridge.
Current-source ordinary-input reference route completes both exits in 2425 frames without death; it is a feasibility result, not a human learning outcome.

timing.rationale: The bridge accumulates collapse time and can fail within 0.8 seconds after Pac leaves STEADY; Isp must reach RESCUE before that support is removed. The visible subtitle gives a clear repeated rule, so this is a sustained handoff window rather than a narrow one-shot reflex.

evidence.claim: Bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds without steady; rescue latch takes over.
Unsupported occupancy drives the collapse timer.
Visible subtitle identifies the endpoint of Pac’s hold.
Early-release record anchors timing at Isp’s first bridge support, before rescue.

hazards.rationale: The mandatory ferry and bridge routes lie above lethal slime. Pac must cross the ferry span; both heroes traverse the bridge span, and the bridge can collapse into slime if the handoff is early. Safe shores and explicit steady/rescue support offer recovery, but the route has repeated real exposure.

evidence.claim: Two slime regions lie directly beneath the ferry and bridge, harming both.
Contact with an active harmful hazard kills.
Premature bridge release ends in death over the mandatory span.

novelty.rationale: Level 03 already teaches Isp bracing a ferry while Pac crosses and a bubble can float Isp off STOP; level 04 teaches Pac stabilizing a bridge until Isp reaches RESCUE. Level 05 recombines those familiar roles into ferry-to-island plus bridge sequence with two slime spans, so it is a new combination of directly taught mechanics.

evidence.claim: Level 03 teaches the ferry/stop/bubble recovery.
Level 04 teaches the steady bridge/rescue handoff.
Current level combines the ferry setup and dangerous bridge transfer.

recovery_cost.rationale: A bubble can release STOP, but Isp can land and brake again without a lethal consequence. By contrast, releasing STEADY before Isp reaches RESCUE causes bridge collapse into slime and a full attempt failure after the pair has completed substantial setup. This severe mistake raises the overall recovery burden.

evidence.claim: Pad recovery, short bridge timer, and lethal slime are defined.
The tested early release results in death.
Correct route completes without death.

solution_clarity.rationale: The exact subtitle says Pac holds STEADY until Isp presses RESCUE, and the pads are visibly labeled, while earlier rooms taught both parts. The auxiliary ferry/bubble/glucose dialogue and idle WINDUP/RECOVER/STUCK labels can compete for attention; the main handoff is clear, but the broader sequence still requires coordinating several cues.

evidence.claim: Visible subtitle gives the central handoff; characters also mention ferry and locked gate.
Start screenshot labels STOP and RESCUE across the route.
WINDUP and RECOVER labels appear in idle state without player action.

control_friction.rationale: No direct two-human keyboard reliability evidence exists. Successful scripted keyboard traces show only that a route can be executed programmatically.

evidence.claim: No novice played; captures were idle and controls were not tested.
Current-source ordinary-input reference route completes both exits in 2425 frames without death; it is a feasibility result, not a human learning outcome.

confidence_reason: Current authored source defines both dangerous crossings and handoff mechanics. A current-source ordinary-input reference completes the route, while a deliberate early-release trace reproduces the bridge-collapse death and distinguishes first bridge contact from the rescue handoff. No human pair was observed, and these traces do not estimate novice discovery or performance.

confirmed: The visible Pac STEADY/Isp RESCUE instruction correctly identifies the central collaboration and its order.
The ferry bubble and locked finish-gate messages are both relevant to the route, but the bubble temporarily affects STOP and RESCUE answers the finish gate/bridge concerns.
The idle STUCK/WINDUP/RECOVER labels were not caused by player input; the source defines automatic bubble interference and attack phases.
missed_mechanics: Isp’s STOP both brakes the motorized ferry and opens Pac’s island barrier; Gem’s bubble can FLOAT Isp off STOP and release that gate until he re-brakes.
Pac must cross to STEADY and maintain it while Isp crosses the bridge all the way to RESCUE; stepping onto the bridge is not the handoff point.
RESCUE is a latch that takes over bridge stabilization and opens Pac’s finish gate so he can follow.
The ferry and bridge each have lethal slime underneath; a premature hold release can drop Isp into slime and kill him.
changed_judgments: Reasoning rises from 2 to 3 because the actual route has a multi-stage ferry/stop, steady bridge, rescue latch dependency, with bubble displacement capable of forcing a re-brake.
Cooperation rises from 2 to 3 because the ferry and bridge require separate hero roles and the second handoff has a fatal timing boundary: Pac must wait until Isp reaches RESCUE.

Execution rises from 2 to 3 because both heroes cross the ferry/bridge route with multiple jump/landing transitions above slime; this rates mandatory movement, not merely visible decorative platforms.
Timing changes from unknown to 2 because the bridge collapses 0.8 seconds after unsupported occupancy; the visible subtitle makes the required endpoint clear, and the correct route is repeatable.
Hazards changes from unknown to 3 because mandatory ferry and bridge crossings are above lethal slime, and the early-release trace confirms bridge-collapse death.
Novelty remains 2: level 03 taught ferry/stop/bubble recovery and level 04 taught steady/rescue bridge handoff; this room recombines both patterns with a second lethal span.
Recovery changes from unknown to 3 because an early bridge handoff causes a full failure after setup, while the separate bubble displacement off STOP can be recovered by re-braking.
Clarity remains 2: the main handoff is explicit, but multiple auxiliary dialogue/dynamic cues may compete with the route instruction.
unresolved: No novice pair has been observed handling the automatic bubble interruption or deciding when to stop holding STEADY.
The deterministic early-release trace shows one fatal mistake but not its frequency or how players read the warning labels.
The reference completion uses long idle/wait intervals; those demonstrate completion feasibility but do not measure real-time player skill or frustration.

single_operator_note: One person would switch between Isp ferry/bridge movement and Pac maintaining STEADY. Pac must hold while Isp moves; switching inputs is an extra coordination burden, but there is no direct one-operator observation and this stays outside the two-human baseline.
